title: Boolean Rounding on Fixed Coordinates
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces, with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to $1$, and let $J$ be a subset of the coordinate indices. Suppose $f,h$ are real-valued functions on the product outcome space, $f$ takes values in $\{-1,1\}$, and $h$ depends only on the coordinates in $J$. Then there is a function $g$ taking values in $\{-1,1\}$ and depending only on the coordinates in $J$ such that $\Pr_P(f\ne g)\leq\mathbb E_P[(f-h)^2]$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space
All coordinate weights are strictly positive and sum to $1$
$J$ is a subset of the coordinate indices
$f,h$ are real-valued on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $J\subseteq[n]$, and functions $f,h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. If $f$ takes values in $\{-1,1\}$ and $h$ depends only on $J$, there exists $g:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on $J$ such that $\Pr_P(f\ne g)\le\mathbb E_P(f-h)^2$.
